concepts.title: Arobinagu — The Feminine Head Of Agwu (Earlier Title: "Arobinagu And The Two-Headed Ogum")
concepts.excerpt: The previous version of this page identified Arobinagu as "the female head of Ogum" — the two-headed deity Ogum, with Ekwensu as the male head.

concepts.title: Akpo and Uche — Dual Streams of Consciousness
concepts.excerpt: You're listening to someone explain a problem. Halfway through, you get an idea — a connection that solves it, a metaphor that lands.

concepts.title: Ekwensu as Discipline and Enforcement Spirit
concepts.excerpt: You make a commitment. I'm going to write every morning at 5am. Day three, you don't want to.

concepts.title: Ogu — The Universe's Force of Justice
concepts.excerpt: In Igbo cosmology, when a man receives a chieftaincy title, he puts a feather in his cap.

concepts.title: Igbo Ancestral Psychology
concepts.excerpt: Odinala has its own system of psychology — documented in Igbo traditional medicine texts — that identifies, categorizes, and provides remedies for psychological disorders.

concepts.title: Jinshin/Doshin — The Dual Mind
concepts.excerpt: The jinshin/doshin framework is Fujibayashi Yasutake's core psychological doctrine, introduced in Seishin I (Volume 2) of the Bansenshukai (1676).

concepts.title: Tapas as Spiritual Catalyst
concepts.excerpt: Tapas (Sanskrit: तपस्, from root tap — "to heat, to burn") is the most ancient named concept for difficulty as spiritual catalyst in the Indian traditions.
